newsitem.title: UK: Nickel prices could hit $10,000 in 1998 - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Nickel prices could hit $10,000 in 1998 - Wolff.

text.p: Nickel prices have already gained some 30 percent since the end of 1996, and further advances are expected for the rest of this year and in 1998, Dr Mo Ahmadzadeh president of Rudolf Wolff and Co Inc said.
In a speech prepared for delivery at the Institute of Scrap Re-cycling Industries (ISRI) annual convention in Las Vegas, Ahmadzadeh said the market may pull back in the short term to around $7,500.
"...but high values around the $9,000/tonne level can be expected this year. In 1998, Wolff expects prices to increase to trade around $10,000/tonne," he said.
Factors that have helped the nickel price run this year have been tightness in stainless-steel scrap after a pick-up in production rates and new capacity at stainless mills.
"In addition, the flow of investment money into the base metals markets has raised questions as to whether there will be a repeat of the 1993-1995 bull run," Ahmadzadeh said.

During the next two years a further 61,000 tonnes of refined nickel is due to come on-stream, but net exports from Eastern countries are seen falling by 26,000 tonnes while Western world consumption is forecast rising by 79,000 tonnes.
"This would suggest a deficit of 44,000 tonnes of nickel," he added.
The projected pick-up in demand will deplete inventories further, while Wolff's forecast of consumption growth is relatively conservative at 4.5 percent.
"If demand exceeds this growth rate inventories will come under further pressure and higher prices may then follow," he added.
